mechanism_narrative: FGFR1 (RTK, active kinase) and TNFRSF1A (TNFR superfamily, death domain, no intrinsic kinase) are forced into proximity by a flexible GS4 linker (~20 Å). FGFR1's tyrosine kinase transphosphorylates TNFRSF1A's intracellular domain, creating phosphotyrosine docking sites for SH2-domain adaptors (GRB2, SHC1, PIK3R1) that normally cannot engage TNFR1. This biases output toward MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT signaling via FRS2-GRB2-SOS1 and FRS2-GAB1-PIK3R1 cascades, while sterically excluding the canonical TNFR1 death-domain complex (TRADD/RIPK1/TRAF2/FADD/CASP8) and its NF-κB/apoptotic outputs. The result is a pro-survival, pro-growth signal that shifts aged muscle toward a younger transcriptional phenotype.
